info.desc: Violator is the seventh album by the English synthpop group Depeche Mode, released by Mute in 1990. Preceded by the hit singles Personal Jesus and Enjoy the Silence (a Top 10 hit on both sides of the Atlantic), Violator propelled the band into international stardom. The album yielded two further hit singles, Policy of Truth and World in My Eyes. This album is the first of the band to achieve the Top 10 on the Billboard 200 (number seven) and stand 74 weeks in the chart. In 2003, the album was ranked number 342 on Rolling Stone magazine's list of .

podcast.body: The period surrounding the "Violator" album in the early 1990s represented a low point for Dave Gahan, marked by an "endless party" tour. By its conclusion, those close to the band observed Gahan on the brink of a breakdown, characterized by anger and irritability, as he struggled to cope with the band's immense success, which included selling millions of albums and concert tickets. "The worst period for Dave was during the era of the violator album in the early 90s. That tour was one endless party."

podcast.body: This album was the subject of an infamous autograph session at The Warehouse music store in Los Angeles on March 20, 1990. The event drew thousands of fans, leading to a riot that required police intervention and resulted in injuries, arrests, and property damage. "One of their stores in Los Angeles was the scene of the infamous Depeche Mode riot during an autograph session for the violator Ravel on March 20th 1990."
